requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM account WHERE account_id = 53 AND name = 'Apex Industries' AND email_domain = 'apex-ind.com' AND account_type = 'customer'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
account_type customer from 'Apex Industries became a customer'

requirements.text: add Sarah Miles (sarah@apex-ind.com) as the primary contact
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 803 AND first_name = 'Sarah' AND last_name = 'Miles' AND email = 'sarah@apex-ind.com' AND role = 'customer'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
implied by the request, not stated: a contact needs a portal user and no user with this name or email exists in the seed
role customer: the policy calls contacts' users portal users (customers), and every contact's user in the seed has role customer

requirements.text: add Sarah Miles (sarah@apex-ind.com) as the primary contact
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contact WHERE contact_id = 125 AND account_id = 53 AND portal_user_id = 803 AND is_primary = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
account_id and portal_user_id are the new account and the new user, each assumed next in sequence

requirements.text: register their production server APX-NGINX-001 as in_use and linked to NGINX Plus
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 301 AND account_id = 53 AND product_id = 11 AND serial_number = 'APX-NGINX-001' AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
NGINX Plus is product 11 by exact name; the 'NGINX Plus Variant' products are other products
no installed product with this serial exists in the seed

requirements.text: set up the active support contract for thirty-five thousand dollars with start_date 18 November 2025
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contract WHERE contract_id = 154 AND account_id = 53 AND contract_type = 'support' AND status = 'active' AND contract_price = 35000 AND start_date = '2025-11-18' AND end_date IN ('2026-11-17', '2026-11-18')
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
end_date from 'a one-year NGINX Plus support contract'; the request does not say whether the last day is 17 or 18 November 2026, so both are accepted

requirements.text: add the premium entitlement with 24/7 coverage and a limit of forty cases per month
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 432 AND account_id = 53 AND support_level = 'premium' AND coverage_hours = 'h24x7' AND max_cases_per_month = 40 AND active = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
active = 1: the policy requires the entitlement for a case's product to be actively running
product_id and contract_id not fixed by request or policy (an account-wide entitlement is allowed), so not tested

requirements.text: open a case directly in in_progress state so the SLA timer starts immediately – priority high, channel phone, short description exactly "NGINX Plus returning 502 Bad Gateway since go-live", attach the server APX-NGINX-001 to the case, and link Sarah Miles as the reporting contact

cells.short_description: NGINX Plus returning 502 Bad Gateway since go-live

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 53 AND contact_id = 125 AND installed_product_id = 301 AND channel = 'phone' AND priority = 'high' AND state = 'in_progress' AND short_description = 'NGINX Plus returning 502 Bad Gateway since go-live'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence
state in_progress from the request's words 'open a case directly in in_progress state'
contact_id and installed_product_id are the new contact and installed product, each assumed next in sequence
product_id not tested: the policy needs a product or an installed product, and the server is attached

requirements.text: open a case directly in in_progress state so the SLA timer starts immediately
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 1233 AND sla_def_id IN (2, 7, 11) AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: implied by the request ('so the SLA timer starts immediately') and the policy rule that a case moving to in progress gets its appropriate SLA
SLA definitions 2, 7 and 11 are the active ones for priority high; at least one must be linked
seed high-priority cases each carry definitions 7 and 11, but the policy does not fix which or how many

Verify state.evidence: the check tests state = 'new', but the request says 'open a case directly in in_progress state so the SLA timer starts immediately'; repaired to in_progress

notes:
The two passes agree on every requirement (account 53, portal user 803, contact 125, installed product 301, contract 154, entitlement 432, case 1233 and its SLA link), every cell and value, and all five dispositions; they differ only in the wording of requirement texts and assumptions, so there is no disagreement to log.
The acting user (user 32) is an admin, so has full access under the policy, but is inactive in the seed; the policy has no rule that stops an inactive user acting, so every requirement assumes the request is carried out.
The policy's default state for a newly registered case is new, and the benchmark's 'Verify state' tests new; the request explicitly asks for in_progress, and the lifecycle allows new to in_progress, so the final state is in_progress and the check is repaired.
New rows are anchored by the next id in each table; the benchmark's checks find the same rows by joining on the account name instead.
Not tested: the entitlement's product_id and contract_id, the case's product_id (the attached installed product carries NGINX Plus), the contact's and user's active flags, and SLA start times, none of which the request or policy fixes.
